title: Opening Night
condition: flag:hall.restored && flag:hall.roof && quest:wren_full_house=done && flag:event.piper_heart10 && flag:event.juno_heart10 && hour>=18 && hour<23 && !festival.in:==0

beats.text: There you are! I closed at five sharp tonight. No sense waiting for one more customer. They're all here!
Checked the roof once. Twice. ...Three times, my father said. It's finished.
Your planks are up there, every one. I've told the word "nearly" it can retire.
Look at this room! Full, and the porch is full too. Somebody count the porch, I've lost track of my own party.
[player]. You brought the wine, I brought the village. First glass is yours.
Okay, okay, okay, the door. Did it squeak? It didn't squeak. Say it didn't squeak.

choice.text: So. Is this the full house I asked for? Be honest. I'll improve it later.

reply.text: Everything I asked for, and a roof I didn't. That's how the story starts. Now, between us, who takes the credit?
Loud, crowded and perfect. I'm stealing that for the story. Somebody write it down before I improve it.

options.text: I counted forty. Then four hundred.

reply.text: Four hundred! By tomorrow it's a thousand, and you were there for every one. You're learning how I tell it. Somebody keep score.

options.text: I'm just glad I'm in it.

reply.text: You're in it. You're the first line, actually. I'll keep your part small, but somebody in this hall is keeping score.

beats.text: The roof's done, the hall's open, and nobody asked for credit. I'm writing it on the slate anyway.
Hm. Good roof. Three.
Big room, new roof, and the finest fiddler in Wetherell. Also the only fiddler. The competition's thin.
First verse, then I step off. I'm calm. I'm holding this fiddle like a hot loaf.

{if choice:chorus.home}Home, home, wherever the lamp is on. ...Your turn, Wetherell.{else}{if choice:chorus.road}The road goes on, and the road comes home. ...Your turn, Wetherell.{else}There's always room, there's always room. ...Your turn, Wetherell.{/if}{/if}

beats.narrate: The whole hall sings the chorus. Piper has stopped playing, and nobody minds.

beats.text: Hm. Hm-hm. I know the tune. Say nothing.
Hear that? Nobody's playing, and it's still going. ...That's a chorus.
Four words, Bram. "I know the tune." Don't worry, I'll say nothing. I'll just tell everyone.
The hall door hangs on hinges I made. My mark's on every pin, and it swings like it's showing off!
First thing I've marked that doesn't live at the forge. Technically it moved out. Technically it's a door.
Wren wanted the porch counted. Six out there, seven in here. Every account in Wetherell, open at once!
The roof pool is closed! Six winters of coins, and Tilda picked the right year. She says it was skill.
Hm. Four. Five. Somebody pay Wren.
Into the hall box, all of it. Marcus, I've put you down for one dance. Collect it now.
On the slate, then. I'll check the roof once more first. Three times, my father said.
Collecting. One dance. Nobody tell the ladder.

beats.narrate: Marcus takes his one dance. Tilda counts the steps for him. The lamps burn low, and nobody goes home.

beats.text: I labeled the door. "Hall Door (Open)." First label I've ever made that I never want to change.
This roof will outlive me. Tonight it only has to outlive the dancing.
Last entry tonight, in the good chalk: "Opening night. Everyone came." That's the only total I ever wanted.

Here's how I'll tell it: the whole village, one roof, nobody in a corner. {if choice:wren.bag.go}And one day I'll tell it somewhere with a sea.{else}{if choice:wren.bag.stay}And I'll tell it right here. I stayed for this.{else}You listened, so you hear it first. I won't even improve it. Much.{/if}{/if}
